chunks: What has happened to you? You may not be guided aright or shown the right path.
Should in these circumstances I go forth? In fact, at this time one of the brave and the valorous among you whom I select should go out.
It does not suit me to leave the army, the city, the public treasury, the land revenue, the dispensation of justice among Muslims and looking after the demands of the claimants,
and to follow one contingent after the other moving here and there like featherless arrow moving in the quiver.
ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Ali say it was not suitable for him to leave the city to lead troops in battle?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) highlights the distinction between the Caliph's administrative duties and the warriors' combat roles, using the metaphor of an arrow in a hollow reed to illustrate the instability of leadership if he were to leave the capital. This passage underscores the Shia scholarly view of the Imam's comprehensive governance (wilayah al-takwiniyah and wilayah al-tashri'iyah), where he manages the state's core institutions while delegating military expeditions to capable commanders. The rhetorical question emphasizes that true leadership requires stability and continuity, not merely personal bravery in the field.
